title: Year two close: the book read through
hookLine: from the Opening to the thirtieth part, the whole Qur'an has now been heard once

lines: YEAR ONE CARRIED THE THIRTIETH PART.
cards: On the first day of this year, your line was: from the opening, onward.

Since then this path has walked from surah one, the Fatiha, through the Cow and the Family of Imran, past Yusuf and Maryam and the Cave, through the Ant and the Stories, all the way to surah seventy-seven.
Year one had already carried the last part, the thirtieth, from seventy-eight to the end. Put the two years together, and something has happened quietly.

teach.h: ALL 114 SURAHS, HEARD AT LEAST ONCE.
teach.b: Every one of the hundred and fourteen surahs has now been heard on this path at least once. The short surahs came whole. The long ones came by theme, a passage and an idea at a time, not every verse read aloud.

teach.h: A FIRST HEARING, NOT A FULL RECITATION.
teach.b: So this is a first hearing, not a full recitation. But it has a shape Muslims know well.
Finishing the Qur'an from beginning to end is called a khatm, a sealing or completing, and it has a long history.
A hadith in al-Bukhari says the angel Jibril went over the Qur'an with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ once every Ramadan, and twice in the year he died.
Many Muslims aim for a khatm each Ramadan; some families and mosques gather to hear its final surahs together and make du'a.
In many communities, the moment one reading ends, the next begins: back to the Fatiha, and the first lines of the Cow. The book has no last page, only a place where you turn around.
The year was built in five blocks: the Opening and the long Medinan surahs; prophets, parables and light; a holy-days interlude; the middle of the book; and the run toward the thirtieth part.
The last month gathered it all: the prophets named, the women remembered, justice, mercy, the earth, and this past week, the prophets' own du'as.

Pickthall's translation of the Fatiha opens: "In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds." That is where the reading began. It is also where the next one starts.

how: Many Muslims complete a reading of the whole Qur'an, a khatm, especially during Ramadan, often closing with a gathering and du'a, and in many communities a new reading begins at once with the Fatiha and the opening of al-Baqarah.

o: finishing the whole Qur'an, start to end
learning the whole Qur'an by heart
a seal stamped on a finished Qur'an

games.q: year two close — tap the pairs.

s: this year read every verse of the long surahs aloud
the long surahs came by theme: a first hearing, not a full recitation.
the Prophet went over the Qur'an with Jibril twice in his final Ramadan
a hadith in al-Bukhari says once a year, and twice in the year he died.
in many communities, a new reading begins as soon as one ends
back to the Fatiha and the opening of the Cow.

games.q: you've just finished the last surah of a full reading of the Qur'an. what do many communities do next?
o: close the book until next year.
games.why: in many communities the next reading starts at once: the Fatiha, then the first lines of the Cow. the book has no last page.

practice: If you pray, recite the Fatiha, in Arabic if you know it, or hear its meaning in English, line by line.
Then bring back one verse from this year that stayed with you, maybe a healing and a mercy, maybe I was wrong, maybe no compulsion, and say it once or simply hold it.
If you don't pray, let one line from the year come back, and notice why that one stayed.

wordCard.voice: Khatm. A sealing, a completing: every surah of the Qur'an now heard once on this path, and a door back to the Fatiha. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: the whole book, heard once. Tomorrow, year three: the people who carried this book. Year two, done.
